summary: This chunk adds new eval-tracking files for the adversarial-review-2 skill workspace. It adds grading.json and two timing.json files recording a baseline (without_skill) run of eval-1 (cache design red-team), which passed all 7 expectations in 120.6s and 33,200 tokens. It also adds eval-2's metadata (an on-call rotation red-team prompt with 6 expectations) and the target artifact for that eval: a follow-the-sun on-call plan with a stated timezone gap, an inexperienced Krakow team, incomplete access provisioning, and a US-only incident-commander pool.

claims.text: The without_skill run for eval-1 (cache-design-redteam) passed all 7 expectations (pass_rate 1.0)
The run-1 execution used 5 tool calls (Read:1, Write:3, Bash:1), 3 steps, 0 errors, and took 120.6 seconds
Total tokens for the run-1 timing.json entry is 33,200 over a duration of 120,606 ms
The without_skill/timing.json (run-level, not run-1) has identical values to run-1/timing.json (33200 tokens, 120606 ms)
The eval_feedback notes the 'or equivalent' clause in the threat-model expectation lets a severity-scale definition pass, so it may not discriminate skill from baseline
Eval-2 (oncall-plan-redteam) has 6 expectations, including a specific timezone-gap claim: Krakow 08:00-20:00 CET equals 02:00-14:00 ET, leaving 20:00-02:00 ET uncovered
The on-call rotation plan's goal is to eliminate overnight pages for the 6-engineer US-East platform team by splitting on-call with a new 3-engineer Krakow team
Krakow covers 08:00-20:00 CET and US-East covers 08:00-20:00 ET, with gaps outside those windows paging 'whichever shift is closest'
The current incident-commander pool is all US-based and stays as-is
The Krakow team joined 6 weeks ago, has not shipped to production, and its access provisioning (prod SSH, dashboards, PagerDuty) is 'in progress'
Runbooks live in the internal wiki and the US team will 'tidy them up' before handover

risks.note: Two timing.json files at different path depths (run-1/ vs the run root) hold byte-identical content; unclear if one is a stray duplicate or an intentional rollup copy.

The plan itself leaves the overnight gap's escalation rule vague/undefined ('closest' is not quantified), which is the kind of gap the eval-2 expectations are designed to catch, but the chunk only shows the plan text, not a review of it.

least_confident: Whether the duplicate timing.json content (run-1/timing.json vs the parent without_skill/timing.json) reflects an intended rollup pattern used elsewhere in this workspace or is simply an accidental duplicate, since this chunk shows no other run's directory structure for comparison.
